land.text: the Palau district of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands: 'Palau was passed formally to the United States under United Nations auspices in 1947'; the Republic of Palau since 1 January 1981

predecessors.note: Chain of rule on the pages: Spanish East Indies (1885), sold to Germany in 1899, the Japanese South Seas Mandate, captured by the US in 1944 after the Battle of Peleliu. The Security Council ended the trusteeship for Palau on 25 May 1994 (Resolution 956); the Compact took effect on 1 October 1994. Cliopatria's United States row (1967-2005) still contains Palau's main cell, so the US dossier must hand Palau over in 1994.

correction.text: 'Palau is divided into sixteen states', with Sonsorol and Hatohobei (Tobi) in the Southwest Islands 'some 604 kilometers (375 miles) from the main islands'

keyframe_review.note: 659 km2 against the infobox 459 km2 (body text 466; ratio 1.43, within a factor of two). The outline (bbox 134.38-134.62E, 7.29-7.61N) is Babeldaob and Koror only; it leaves out Kayangel, Peleliu, Angaur and the Southwest Islands, which the page names. At the gazetteer's grid the country polygon equals the Cliopatria shape (1 land cell); adding Hatohobei gives 2. Peleliu, Angaur, Kayangel and Sonsorol are real admin-1 units that resolve to 0 cells at this grid.

correction.text: the sixteen states including the Southwest Islands, as for 1996-2023 (same outline in Cliopatria)

keyframe_review.note: Same outline and area as the 1996 shape; same correction.

region.text: the Palau district of the Trust Territory, now 'sixteen states'

ledger.note: 1994: Palau becomes independent in free association with the United States. 'The compact entered into force on 1 October 1994, concluding Palau's transition from trusteeship to independence'; the Republic of Palau had been established on 1 January 1981 and UN admission followed on 15 December 1994.
2006: the capital moves from Koror to Ngerulmud in Melekeok state. 'It replaced Koror City as the capital in October 2006'; the complex 'was officially opened on 7 October 2006'.

certainty.note: Island coasts; maritime limits are not drawn. The page says Palau 'shares maritime boundaries' with the Federated States of Micronesia, Indonesia and the Philippines, and patrols a 600,000 km2 exclusive economic zone.

notes: Cliopatria rows. The Palau row starts 1996 although independence was 1 October 1994 (keyframe added); its outline is Babeldaob and Koror only (one grid cell), so the shapes are corrected to the country plus Hatohobei. Cliopatria's United States row 1967-2005 contains Palau's cell, so the US dossier (am-07) should end the Trust Territory in 1994. The Palau page dates the trusteeship 18 July 1947 (the Trust Territory page agrees; the FSM page says 2 April 1947); it gives no date for the Japanese mandate or for the Peleliu battle beyond 1944. The identity start follows independence (1 October 1994); the Republic of Palau of 1 January 1981 was still a trust territory. The grid cannot represent most of the state's islands (Peleliu, Angaur, Kayangel and Sonsorol resolve to 0 cells), which the gazetteer agent should know. Needed from oc-02-x: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (1947-1994) and the South Seas Mandate (1920-1945). Page budget: three pages for Palau (the Ngerulmud page settles the capital), pooled with the FSM within the group's ten.
